objectives.description: Explains a fraction as a number of equal-sized parts of one whole.
Explains why two fractions can name the same amount (e.g. 1/2 and 2/4).
Compares unit fractions by reasoning about the size of the parts.

levels.0: Describes a fraction as two unrelated numbers.
levels.1: Describes parts of a whole but accepts unequal parts.
levels.2: Describes counting parts of a whole without stating the parts must be equal.
levels.3: Explains the denominator as equal parts of one whole and the numerator as how many are counted.

levels.0: Says equivalent fractions are different amounts because the numbers differ.
levels.1: Uses an invalid rule, such as adding the same number to top and bottom.
levels.2: Correctly states two fractions are equal but gives no reason.
levels.3: Explains equivalence by multiplying/dividing both parts or by the same amount of the whole.

levels.0: Compares without reasoning or picks the wrong fraction without explanation.
levels.1: Says a larger denominator means a larger fraction.
levels.2: Picks the correct fraction but explains only partially.
levels.3: Explains that more parts of the same whole means each part is smaller.

misconceptions.description: Accepts unequal parts as fractions of a whole.
Believes adding the same number to numerator and denominator keeps a fraction equal.
Believes a larger denominator always means a larger fraction.

questions.prompt: What does the fraction 3/4 mean? You can describe a picture or an example.
hints: Imagine one pizza. What do the 4 and the 3 tell you about it?

questions.prompt: A pizza is cut into 4 pieces of very different sizes and you eat one piece. Did you eat exactly 1/4 of the pizza? Why or why not?
Are 1/2 and 2/4 the same amount? How do you know?
hints: Picture a rectangle split into 2 parts, then split each part in half again.

questions.prompt: Someone says 2/3 equals 3/4 because they added 1 to the top and the bottom. Do you agree? Explain.
Which is larger, 1/3 or 1/5? Explain your reasoning.
hints: Think about sharing the same cake among 3 people versus among 5 people.

questions.prompt: Would you rather have 1/3 or 1/8 of the same chocolate bar? Why?
